sections.title: Walk the flowchart
sections.intro: A deploy of `orders-api` just went out and the pods won't stay up. Narrow it down from what kubelet recorded, not from guesses.

questions.prompt: What does this output already prove, before you read a single log?
questions.snippet:
NAME              READY   STATUS             RESTARTS      AGE
orders-api-6f9-q   0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   4 (50s ago)   3m
options: The readiness probe is keeping it out
It started at least once and exited — a crash problem
The image couldn't be pulled to the node
The scheduler couldn't place the pod
questions.explanation: RESTARTS > 0 is proof that it ran. That rules out every scheduler, image, and config-resolution cause from file 01.

questions.prompt: In `kubectl describe pod`, which detail splits this problem in half, and how?
options: Which node the pod was placed on
How long it ran — the `Started` to `Finished` gap
The image digest the node actually pulled
Which labels the ReplicaSet added
questions.explanation: One number from data you already have. Immediate deaths mean the app never finished starting: bad command, missing config. Delayed deaths mean it started fine and something happened later: memory, probes, a specific event.

questions.prompt: Here's what you find. Which branch, and what's the next command?
questions.snippet:
Last State:  Terminated
  Reason:    Error
  Exit Code: 1
  Started:   Sat, 25 Oct 2026 09:14:02
  Finished:  Sat, 25 Oct 2026 09:14:03
options: After a while — check memory usage
After a while — tune the liveness probe
Immediate — `kubectl logs <pod>`, no flag
Immediate — `kubectl logs <pod> --previous`
questions.explanation: One second of runtime and exit 1 means the app errored during startup. `--previous` matters: without it you get the *current* container, which may have just started and printed nothing yet.

questions.prompt: The previous logs say this. What's your diagnosis, and what do you check in the deploy?
questions.snippet:
Error: required environment variable DATABASE_URL is not set
    at loadConfig (/app/config.js:12)
options: Code and config were rolled out out of sync
The image layers are corrupt
The database is down for maintenance
The node is out of memory
questions.explanation: The app says what's wrong in plain words. "Just went out" plus a config error almost always means the code and its config were rolled out out of sync.

questions.prompt: Fixed. A week later the pods crash again, but differently. Which branch is this, and what does 137 mean?
questions.snippet:
Last State:  Terminated
  Reason:    OOMKilled
  Exit Code: 137
  Started:   09:00:11
  Finished:  09:47:52
options: Neither — the node rebooted underneath it
After a while — the liveness probe killed it
Immediate — a startup bug in the new build
After a while — it hit its memory limit (SIGKILL)
questions.explanation: 47 minutes of runtime puts this in the resource/runtime branch. The Reason field is what separates an OOM kill from any other SIGKILL. Exit 137 on its own isn't enough.

questions.prompt: Your teammate suggests doubling the memory limit. What do you want to know first?
options: Is usage leaking upward, or steady just above the limit?
Is the pod's restartPolicy set to Always?
Is the image tag the latest release?
Is the node's CPU saturated right now?
questions.explanation: `kubectl top pod` over time, or your metrics dashboards, shows the trend. A higher limit with a leak behind it just crashes later and squeezes everything else on the node in the meantime.

questions.prompt: Another service's pods restart about 40 seconds after every start, forever. There's no OOM, and the logs show it's still booting when it dies. Events show this. What's the real fix?
questions.snippet:
Warning  Unhealthy  kubelet  Liveness probe failed: Get "http://10.1.2.3:8080/healthz": connection refused
Normal   Killing    kubelet  Container billing failed liveness probe, will be restarted
options: Raise the memory limit so it boots faster
Remove the liveness probe entirely
Add a `startupProbe` so liveness waits for boot
Set `restartPolicy: Never` on the Deployment
questions.explanation: kubelet is doing the killing, not the app. Removing the probe would also stop it from catching real hangs later, and a Deployment can't use `restartPolicy: Never` anyway. The startupProbe is built for exactly this case.

questions.prompt: Last check before you sign off: a `nightly-export` pod shows exit code 0, Reason `Completed`, and keeps restarting. Bug in the app?
options: Yes — exit 0 here means it was killed
No — the liveness probe is misconfigured
No — it succeeded; it belongs in a Job
Yes — a service shouldn't ever exit
questions.explanation: Nothing failed, so there's no bug to chase. The fix is a design change: move it to a Job, which allows `OnFailure`/`Never`.

sections.title: Read the signal
sections.intro: Each one stands alone. Read the exit code or event, and say what it means.

questions.prompt: The pod spec is `command: ["sh", "-c", "start-server --port 8080"]`. What happened?
questions.snippet:
Exit Code: 127
$ kubectl logs api --previous
sh: start-server: not found
options: Port 8080 is already taken in the pod
The image doesn't contain `sh` at all
The container ran out of memory
`start-server` isn't on the shell's PATH
questions.explanation: 127 means a shell was involved and couldn't find what it was told to run. If `sh` itself were missing, the runtime would fail before anything ran (CreateContainerError / StartError), not with 127.

questions.prompt: The file definitely exists in the image. Why might exec still say "no such file"?
questions.snippet: exec /app/start.sh: no such file or directory
options: Its permissions aren't executable
Its interpreter is missing (shebang or CRLF)
It's in the wrong directory in the image
The node's disk is full
questions.explanation: The kernel reports the missing shebang interpreter as if the script itself were missing. Its cousin `exec format error` means an image built for the wrong CPU architecture.

questions.prompt: Exit code 137, but `Reason: Error`, not OOMKilled. What killed it?
options: The app called exit(137) itself
A non-OOM SIGKILL — often a liveness restart
A network timeout inside the app
An OOM kill — 137 always means memory
questions.explanation: Exit codes above 128 mean "killed by signal (code − 128)". 137 is SIGKILL from any source. 143 (SIGTERM) means the app shut down cleanly when asked.

questions.prompt: A pod shows `READY 0/1`, `RESTARTS 0`, and its readiness probe is failing. Is this CrashLoopBackOff territory?
options: No — readiness never restarts anything
Yes — the probe will restart it soon
Yes — readiness and liveness act the same
No — it's actually still Pending
questions.explanation: Only liveness failures restart a container. If RESTARTS isn't climbing, readiness is the more likely issue. Find out what the readiness endpoint is waiting on.

questions.prompt: STATUS is `CreateContainerError` with RESTARTS 0. Does it belong in this file?
questions.snippet: Warning  Failed  kubelet  Error: failed to create containerd task: exec: "/app/server": executable file not found in $PATH
options: Not really — RESTARTS 0 means it never ran
No — it's a liveness probe problem
Yes — it's crashing on every start
Yes — it's an out-of-memory loop
questions.explanation: The RESTARTS rule decides which file you're in. The fix is still to correct `command`/`args` or the image, but you'd never find this in `--previous` logs, because there aren't any.

questions.prompt: A pod has been crashing for an hour, but it seems to restart only every few minutes now. Did it get better?
options: No — that's the backoff, capped at 5 minutes
No — the scheduler is delaying restarts
Yes — the crashes are getting rarer
No — the node is throttling its CPU
questions.explanation: The "BackOff" in CrashLoopBackOff is the waiting between attempts. The crash itself hasn't changed. Check `--previous` for the most recent death.

questions.prompt: A Job's pod failed three times and then stopped retrying. Is something broken?
options: Not necessarily — Jobs stop at `backoffLimit`
Yes — the controller-manager is down
Yes — it ran out of namespace quota
Yes — it should restart like a Deployment
questions.explanation: Jobs and Deployments handle restarts differently. A Job giving up is correct behavior; a Deployment never gives up.
